## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline stuck-task resurrection MEDIUM (core, session, runtime, capability, hooks)

- **What**: Cline v4.1.26 / v0.0.49 / v3.0.74 / SDK v0.2.0 merged PR #15244: fix orphaned runs from stalling sessions. Previously, starting a session that already had a run in flight replaced its runtime — the original run kept going unreachable (Stop and the queue went to the replacement) and its transcript writes landed on the replacement's stale snapshot. `startSession` now reattaches to the live session instead, and rejects a start that carries a prompt while a run is in progress. A capability request raised after its owner client unregistered (a run still in flight when the desktop sidecar restarted) waited forever: nothing could answer it and nothing timed it out. The hub now records every client that registered each capability for a session, including clients that join a running task, and sends a request to the first one still connected. When none is left, the request fails fast with a message the user can act on. The desktop registered `beforeModel/beforeTool/afterTool` hooks only to hold a run while the mistake-limit prompt was open. They were no-ops otherwise, but each one round-tripped hub → sidecar on every model and tool call and tied every desktop run to the sidecar staying connected. `SessionRuntime` now holds those same boundaries on its pending mistake-tracker work, in-process, so `onConsecutiveMistakeLimitReached` pauses the run by itself. The desktop keeps the callback and drops the three hooks: a run no longer depends on the sidecar between steps and survives an app restart. A run's hooks and client tools stay with the app that started it. If that app disconnects or leaves the task, its pending requests are cancelled and later ones fail immediately rather than going to whichever app joined later, which may enforce different rules under the same name. Each case emits `task.capability_owner_gone` so tracking can show how often it happens.

- **Why**: Alexi CLI runs sessions in-process (no hub/sidecar split), but the same orphaned-run vulnerability exists when multiple `alexi chat` processes target the same session (two terminals, or one SIGKILL'd mid-run while another resumes). Audit `src/core/sessionManager.ts` for: (1) whether `startSession` / `resumeSession` can replace a live run's runtime (Cline's bug), (2) whether capability requests (tool calls, MCP server calls) have a timeout when the provider/tool is unreachable (Cline's forever-wait bug), (3) whether in-progress runs survive a parent-process SIGKILL (graceful shutdown hooks). Fix: reattach to live session instead of replacing runtime, add capability-request timeout (default 30s, configurable), add process-exit cleanup that marks runs as interrupted instead of leaving them dangling. Test: two `alexi chat` processes on same session, SIGKILL one mid-tool-call, verify the other can resume without stale transcript. Size MEDIUM ~4-6h (audit + test + fix if gap confirmed). Priority MEDIUM (heisenbug, not user-reported but prevents multi-process safety).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15244 (Cline stuck-task fix), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionManager.ts (Alexi session management), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (Alexi run loop)

- **Category**: tool (session, runtime, capability, hooks)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~4-6h. Audit Alexi session manager for orphaned-run vulnerability (multiple processes, SIGKILL mid-run), add reattach logic + capability timeout + exit cleanup if gap confirmed, test multi-process safety.

#### 2. SST catalog-once-per-release bundling HIGH (providers, catalog, startup, perf)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #59173 merged: fetch the models.dev catalog once per release and verify the bundled copy at runtime. Previously, every cold start fetched the catalog from models.dev (adds ~500ms latency, increases models.dev load, fails when offline). Now, a build-time script fetches the catalog, writes it to `catalog-snapshot.json`, and the runtime verifies the snapshot's ETag / integrity at startup (HTTP 304 → keep cached, 200 → replace). Reduces cold-start latency by ~500ms and models.dev load by 100% (only revalidation requests, not full fetches). Snapshot generation is gated by `BUILD_CATALOG_SNAPSHOT=1` so local dev builds skip it (faster). Runtime checks the snapshot's `fetchedAt` timestamp and revalidates if older than 7 days (configurable `CATALOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS`). If revalidation fails (offline, models.dev down), keeps the bundled snapshot as fallback. Ports upstream pattern from kilocode `kilo-docs` (catalog caching).

- **Why**: Alexi `src/providers/modelCatalog.ts` already fetches SAP AI Core deployment catalog at startup (`refreshModelCatalog`), with a 5-minute TTL background refresh (`CATALOG_TTL_MS`). Bundling a snapshot reduces cold-start latency and SAP AI Core load: (1) generate `sap-catalog-snapshot.json` at build time (or weekly CI job) via `DeploymentApi.deploymentQuery({ status: 'RUNNING' })`, (2) bundle it into `dist/providers/`, (3) at startup, verify the snapshot's `fetchedAt` timestamp (if older than 7 days, revalidate with SAP), (4) if revalidation fails (offline, SAP down), keep the bundled snapshot as fallback. Adds ETag support to catalog fetching (port SST's ETag header handling). Test: bundle a 7-day-old snapshot, start Alexi offline, verify static fallback works. Size MEDIUM-HIGH ~6-8h (bundle generation script + snapshot verification + ETag support + test coverage + CI integration). Priority HIGH (user-visible cold-start latency reduction, reduces SAP load).

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/59173 (SST catalog bundling), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/modelCatalog.ts (Alexi catalog fetching), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts (static ORCHESTRATION_MODELS)

- **Category**: provider (catalog, startup, perf)

- **Size**: MEDIUM-HIGH ~6-8h. Generate `sap-catalog-snapshot.json` at build time, bundle into dist/, verify at startup with ETag revalidation, fallback to bundled snapshot on failure, add CI job to refresh weekly.

#### 3. SST Bedrock Converse typed options SMALL (providers, bedrock, options)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #59171 merged: add typed Bedrock Converse options (guardrails, inferenceConfig, additionalModelRequestFields). Previously, Bedrock Converse provider accepted a generic `options` object (no type safety, no autocomplete). Now, `BedrockConverseOptions` type defines: `guardrailConfig?: { guardrailIdentifier: string; guardrailVersion: string; trace?: 'enabled' | 'disabled' }`, `inferenceConfig?: { maxTokens?: number; temperature?: number; topP?: number; stopSequences?: string[] }`, `additionalModelRequestFields?: Record<string, unknown>`. Ports upstream AWS SDK types. Enables guardrail enforcement (content filtering, PII detection) and per-request inference tuning without SDK version mismatches.

- **Why**: Alexi `src/providers/` has SAP AI Core routing to Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Mistral/DeepSeek models, but no direct Bedrock integration (SAP may route to Bedrock under the hood, not exposed to Alexi). If SAP AI Core exposes Bedrock routing, add Bedrock provider tuning options: (1) create `src/providers/bedrock-options.ts` with `BedrockConverseOptions` type, (2) forward options to SAP orchestration layer (if supported), (3) document in `docs/PROVIDERS.md`. Conditional on SAP AI Core exposing Bedrock routing. Size SMALL ~2-3h (provider options passthrough + docs + test). Priority LOW (Bedrock not yet confirmed in SAP routing).

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/59171 (SST Bedrock options), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts (Alexi SAP routing), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/docs/PROVIDERS.md (Alexi provider docs)

- **Category**: provider (bedrock, options)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h. Add Bedrock Converse provider options (guardrails, inferenceConfig, additionalModelRequestFields) if SAP AI Core exposes Bedrock routing. Conditional on SAP routing support.

#### 5. SST credential refresh coordination REFERENCE-ONLY (core, auth, multi-process)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #54023 merged: coordinate credential refreshes across locations and processes. Previously, every OpenCode process (CLI, desktop, server) refreshed credentials independently (OAuth tokens, API keys). When multiple processes started at the same time (e.g. 5 desktop windows), all 5 fetched tokens simultaneously (thundering herd, rate-limit risk). Now, a lock file coordinates refreshes: first process acquires the lock, refreshes, writes the new token, releases. Other processes wait on the lock (timeout 10s, then fall back to independent refresh if lock holder crashes). Ports upstream pattern from VS Code remote-SSH (lock-based token coordination).

- **Why**: Alexi is a single-user CLI (no multi-process token sharing today). Pattern is REFERENCE-ONLY for future multi-tenant or multi-user support (e.g. Alexi server mode with multiple clients, or daemon mode with multiple CLI frontends). If Alexi adds multi-process credential caching, port SST's lock-based coordination. Size N/A (reference-only, Alexi currently single-user CLI). Priority N/A (no multi-process credential sharing today).

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/54023 (SST credential coordination), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/auth.ts (Alexi auth layer)

- **Category**: N/A (core, auth, multi-process, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Reference-only pattern for multi-process credential coordination. Alexi currently single-user CLI (no multi-process token sharing).

#### 6. Kilocode transcript selection + MCP SSE scope SKIP (vscode, mcp, sse, regression)

- **What**: Kilocode v7.8.18 merged PR #15472: fix transcript selection in VS Code 1.143 (keep selection on copy, VS Code extension-specific). MCP SSE probe scope fixes (PR merged earlier, follow-up in commit log): narrow SSE probe to stream request only, excluding OAuth discovery. Previously, the origin-wide check let the probe rewrite same-origin OAuth discovery: the SDK merges user-configured MCP headers into discovery requests, so an Accept header that includes `text/event-stream` passed the SSE check and valid JSON metadata became a 405. Now, normalize only the stream request: a GET to the exact endpoint, or to a same-origin redirect target recorded from that request's 3xx response and consumed by the hop the SDK follows. Add regression tests for SDK discovery with the configured header, a same-origin JSON GET at a custom metadata path, and a two-hop redirect chain. SDK 1.32.1 follows same-origin redirects itself and calls the custom fetch again with the redirect target. The probe compared the full request URL to the endpoint, so a 200 non-SSE body at the target passed through and the transport reconnected forever. Compare origins instead; the Accept check still keeps OAuth requests out.

- **Why**: VS Code transcript selection fix is extension-specific (SKIP). MCP SSE probe scope fix is a regression fix for Alexi's existing MCP transport layer (`src/mcp/`). Alexi already has SSE probe logic in `src/mcp/` (check if it has the same origin-wide bug). If yes, port the same-origin + redirect-aware probe from Kilocode. Size SMALL ~1-2h (audit + port if gap confirmed). Priority LOW (MCP SSE edge case, not user-reported). SKIP for now (no user-reported MCP SSE probe bugs in Alexi).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15472 (Kilocode transcript selection), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode commit log (MCP SSE probe scope), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/ (Alexi MCP transport)

- **Category**: N/A (vscode, mcp, sse, regression, skip)

- **Size**: SKIP. VS Code transcript selection is extension-specific. MCP SSE probe scope fix is a regression fix for an edge case not yet reported in Alexi.
